text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate + token latency spike observed on cb-serving-prod (continuous-batching). Alert: 11:50 UTC. Metric: 5xx-rate +700% over baseline and p95 token-latency doubled.

sam: seeing rapid queue growth on node pool A, microbatch sizes stuck at 32 even though traffic spiked. also kv-cache eviction rate shot up.

maria: confirmed: KV cache counters show mass evictions — small request prefixes causing cache churn. suspect prefetch + small microbatches interacting badly under 2500rps.

alex: tagging oncall. is this customer-facing? any active tails?

jess: support: three customers reported degraded responses (chatty assistants timing out). CS says started ~11:48 and affects EU region.

sam: reproducing locally with load generator — continuous batching runtime enters a churn loop: microbatch assemble latency increases -> queueing -> clients time out -> more concurrent retries.

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/continuous-batching#kv-eviction-blowups

maria: quick mitigation proposal: reduce max_microbatch_size from 64->16 on cb-serving-prod pools, temporarily disable aggressive prefetch heuristics (prefetch.enabled=false), and increase kv-cache TTL to favor retention.

alex: agree. Can we patch config via k8s rollout patch to apply to pool labels cb-prod-eu?

sam: preparing a small hotfix configmap:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  max_microbatch_size: "16"
  prefetch.enabled: "false"
  kvcache.ttl_seconds: "300"
```
Applying to cb-prod-eu first.

jess: coordinating with support for customer comms: will draft a notice saying degraded latency and partial timeouts, ETA unknown — we will update in 30m.

ops-bot: applied configmap patch to cb-prod-eu (canary nodes). Rolling update started (pods will drain gracefully).

sam: canary metrics look promising: queue depth down 60%, p95 token-latency back to baseline on canary. No 5xx on canary.

maria: rolling to remaining pools now, doing staggered batches to avoid mass eviction wave.

incident-bot: Pager auto-escalation suppressed by oncall update.

peter: support-sre checking logs for customer-level impact. so far three top customers had 10-20% request failures, we will flag for credit review once incidents closed.

alex: keeping an eye on tail latency. If we still see microbursting after rollout, plan B is to enable adaptive-batching backpressure (throttle-new-requests=true) for heavy-tenancy customers.

sam: rollout complete across all cb-serving-prod nodes at 12:05 UTC. Metrics: 5xx down to baseline, p95 token-latency 0.95x baseline, eviction-rate normalized.

jess: support update posted to customers: short blip of degraded responses 11:48-12:05 UTC, region EU impacted, mitigation applied.

maria: root cause (prelim): an interaction between prefetch heuristics and high concurrency causing many tiny prefixes to be cached and evicted rapidly — that drove KV cache churn which amplified batching delays. The config change reduces microbatch sizes and candidate prefetches so cache stabilization occurs.

ops-bot: creating follow-up run: cb-prefetch-surge-postmortem. Owners: sam, maria, alex. Due: 48h.

support-sre: logging customer cases + attaching timestamps for credits.

aplex: note for next deploy: add an automated canary threshold that blocks prefetch.enabled=true when eviction-rate > X for 5m.

sam: also we should instrument per-tenant prefetch footprint; multi-tenant hot prefixes were the main culprit.

maria: agreed — adding per-tenant cache-usage counters to the telemetry backlog.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 12:07 UTC. Please file full postmortem and QA the adaptive-batching fallback logic.

jess: assigning post-incident comms to me and sam. will sync with CS and legal if any escalations.

sam: quick checklist appended:
- confirm kvcache TTL rollback schedule (we kept 300s temporarily)
- patch prefetch heuristics test in CI to include high-concurrency scenario
- add canary gating for prefetch toggles

maria: logging action items to tracking board. thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:
